extracted.name: Rajma Kebab Sandwich￼
extracted.description: Say hello to my Rajma Kebab Sandwich – a burst of delicious flavors in your mouth!😋 ✅Imagine this: a Rajma kebab spiced to perfection, topped with a slice of cheese, fresh tomato slices, crunchy onion, tangy pickled purple cabbage, and creamy avocado slices, And the magic touch? A dollop of Bengali kasundi mustard, a drizzle of ketchup, all nestled on a bed of crispy lettuce. This sandwich is a flavor-packed delight that will leave you feeling so satisfied! #sandwichitwithmish
ingredient_lines: 2 cans red kidney beans (reduced sodium) or 3/4 cup dry red kidney beans soaked overnight
A few lettuce leaves- butter lettuce romaine, leafy, iceberg all work
3 tablespoons white or apple cider vinegar (for the pickled cabbage)
3 teaspoons sugar or sugar substitute (for the pickled cabbage)
Take the half a head of finely sliced purple cabbage, add 3 teaspoons vinegar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 3 teaspoons sugar or sugar substitute. (I used monkfruit sugar), mix well. Refrigerate overnight
instruction_lines: Set out all your ingredients for ease of cooking. Drain the liquid from the red kidney bean (rajma) cans and wash the beans well. If you’re using dry beans, then soak the beans overnight. Next morning, cook the beans in a pressure cooker or on the stove top till tender.
Add the red kidney beans to a blender along with salt, coriander powder, ginger, garlic, cilantro and blend to a paste. You can add a little water if needed.
In a dry grinder, (I use a coffee grinder), grind the oatmeal to a powder. It’ll take probably take two pulses or three.
Transfer the spiced and blended red kidney bean (rajma) mixture onto a plate and add the oatmeal flour as needed to form a dough. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Use your hands to form big dough balls and flatten them out a little bit and then put them in between parchment paper to flatten them out even further into flat circular shapes (patties).
Now let’s assemble the sandwich! Gather your sandwich and place on a flat surface or a plate.
First, add a ayer of lettuce.
Now, a layer of ketchup, if you would like. I like it!
Next, a slice of cheese. (American, Monterey Jack cheddar provolone all work).
Follow that with a layer of red crunchy onion.
Top that off with a couple slices of tomatoes.
Next up, drizzle some Bengali mustard called kasundi, if you can get your hands on it. Otherwise, you can use any mustard.
Now, add a generous layer of pickled cabbage.
Top that off with a few slices of avocado.
Cover with the top half of the sandwich bun and you are ready to dig in! Enjoy!
